text: Every flow so far has worked only with whatever a trigger or action handed it directly. Castlebridge Logistics needs more than that — a running count, a growing list, a flag that has to survive across many separate steps in the same flow. That's exactly what a variable gives you: a named container you create yourself, instead of a value you can only read.

Every variable starts with the Initialize variable action. Search "variable" in the Add an action box, and pick Initialize variable from the list that comes back. It's a built-in action, not tied to any connector, which means it's available in every single flow you build, regardless of what triggers it.

Configuring it takes three fields: a name, a type — string, integer, float, boolean, array, or object — and an optional starting value. Always set that starting value as a habit, so you know exactly where your variable begins before anything else in the flow touches it. And remember one real restriction: Initialize variable only works at the flow's top level, never inside a condition, a loop, or a scope.

Once a variable exists, four other actions change it. Set variable replaces its value anywhere in the flow. Increment and decrement add or subtract a number, for integers and floats only. And append to string or array variable adds a new value onto the end rather than replacing it — which is exactly how Castlebridge Logistics counts flagged shipments as a loop runs. Increment a counter once per flagged item, and it keeps climbing across every single iteration.

Hold onto that counting pattern — initialize once at the top, then update repeatedly inside the loop. Next up, lesson seven: writing expressions that transform the data a flow carries, instead of just passing it through unchanged.
